exposure: suture type (non-locking continuous, locking continuous, interrupted)
cohort: The study included 52 patients evaluated 6 weeks post-C-section performed in 'Saint Pantelimon' Hospital in Bucharest, Romania.
finding: The use of continuous locking sutures for uterine closure in the first layer was significantly associated with the development of a uterine niche, including all instances of severe niches, compared with continuous non-locking suture or interrupted suture.
